cohort: The study included 107 six-week postpartum primiparous mothers (54 vaginal deliveries, 53 cesarean sections) and 42 healthy nulliparous women.
finding: Pregnancy and childbirth significantly increased bladder detrusor muscle thickness, urethrovesical angle, bladder neck mobility, puborectalis muscle hiatus area, and puborectalis muscle hiatus circumference, with an increased risk of POP associated with a higher number of pregnancies and maternal obesity.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery led to a notably more pronounced elevation in bladder detrusor muscle thickness, urethrovesical angle, bladder neck mobility, puborectalis muscle hiatus area, and puborectalis muscle hiatus circumference compared to other delivery methods.
